notes: v2 (26 Sep 2026 review): S9 new-price series ends when retail ends (2020Q1); LHR is news-only in the alpha; added heat_per_unit_garage (flag F7). Prices are USD per complete unit (GPU rigs = 6 GPUs + frame/PSU/board). Used = healthy second-hand unit. In boom quarters used can exceed new because new units carry a lead time.

models.name: GPU Rig Gen 1
models.why: The card of the 2017 shortage: best MH per $ (MSRP $229, street $350–450 mid-2017). A GTX 1070 rig gives similar hashrate for more money.

power_kw.source: ~135 W per card at the wall, tuned, ×6 + ~140 W platform (≈)

noise_db.source: open-frame rig with 6 axial GPU fans, 55–65 dB at 1 m (≈)

lifespan_years.source: fans and thermal pads degrade in 2–4 years of 24/7 load (≈)

annual_failure_rate.source: ≈ mining forum and hosting anecdotes: fans, risers, PSUs; used ×1.5

models.price_source: RX 580 MSRP $229 (AMD, Apr 2017); street prices via Tom's Hardware / PCPartPicker history and the Tom's Hardware eBay GPU price index 2021–22 (≈)

models.name: GPU Rig Gen 2
models.real_basis: 6× Nvidia RTX 3060 Ti (non-LHR, ~60 MH/s at ~120 W)
models.why: The efficiency sweet spot of Nvidia's Ampere generation and the most-mined card of 2021. Launched 1 Dec 2020 at $399 MSRP.

power_kw.source: ~125 W per card at the wall ×6 + ~100 W platform (≈)

models.lhr_note: LHR (Lite Hash Rate) cards shipped from late May 2021 at ~50% ETH hashrate; software unlocked ~70% (Aug 2021) and ~100% (May 2022). Alpha decision: news item only (news.2021Q2.1). Gen 2 prices already reflect the premium for non-LHR cards. Candidate post-alpha mechanic.
models.price_source: 3060 Ti MSRP $399 (Nvidia, Dec 2020); eBay averages ~$800–1,000 mid-2021 → ~$350 Sep 2022 (Tom's Hardware GPU price index) (≈)

models.name: Antminer S9

annual_failure_rate.source: ≈ hosts report 5–15%/yr hashboard issues on aged S9s

models.price_source: Bitmain shop batches 2017 ($1,265–2,320); secondary-market quotes (Kaboomracks, ASIC Miner Value archive) and Hashrate Index ASIC Price Index '>68 J/TH' tier from 2020 (≈)

models.name: Antminer S19 Pro

annual_failure_rate.source: ≈ early batches had hashboard and PSU issues

models.price_source: Launch ~$2,400–2,800 (Bitmain, May 2020); Hashrate Index ASIC Price Index '<38 J/TH' tier: ~$20/TH mid-2020 → ~$95–105/TH Oct–Nov 2021 → ~$25–30/TH Sep 2022 (≈, read from published charts)
models.lead_time_source: Bitmain futures batches sold 6–9 months forward during 2021; Riot/Marathon 10-Q purchase schedules (≈)

infrastructure_per_mw.note: Excludes the site build (see sites.json capex)

garage_heat_note: heat_per_unit_garage applies only at the garage tier (flag F7): 3 S9s add +24 Heat, so ASICs in a garage trigger neighbour complaints fast. Other tiers use the site's heat_base.
